source.authors: Konstantin M. Engel; Patrik O. Willi; Robert N. Grass; Wendelin J. Stark
source.title: An automated platform for ‘on-demand’ high-speed catalyst synthesis by flame spray pyrolysis

extraction: Manual transcription of six numeric contaminant measurements in four rows of publisher Table 1, verified in indexed primary-publisher text. Resource durations are transcribed from indexed Sections 3.2 and 4.3. No measurements were digitized from a figure or estimated from a chart.
verification_scope: Publisher full-page fetch and direct supplementary PDF download were blocked or unavailable in this environment. Indexed publisher article text exposes the complete Table 1 and the stated timing sentences. The underlying Zenodo experimental files and clocked supplementary run traces were not retrieved. Do not imply that those raw traces were inspected.
limits: The authors state that the contaminant concentrations are close to analytical limits of quantification and require cautious interpretation.
Unreported table cells are missing, not measured zero.
The reported contaminant mol% is relative to the main phase. It is not the same quantity as the benchmark's retained fraction rho, and is not converted into rho here.
These oxide-synthesis measurements do not calibrate carryover in the separate photovoltaic formulation dataset.
The article reports one standard cleaning sequence, not a wash-response curve from which eta or a worst-case carryover bound can be estimated.
The two to three-minute handling range and campaign times are not a fully itemized cost of an assay, fresh preparation or additional wash.
AutoFSP parallelizes operations. Additive action costs are not automatically equivalent to marginal elapsed campaign time.

The Zn trace in C4-S3 is not present in the listed immediately preceding recipe. This motivates caution about a single-predecessor explanation, but near-LOQ measurement and other contamination sources prevent a firm causal attribution.
appropriate_use: Empirical materials context and a constraint on how simulation scales are described; not validation of the proposed policy, not a fitted wash-retention law, and not a physical guarantee.
